name: Creamy Parmesan Pork Chops Skillet

conditions_fit.note: 571 cal within 400-650; 7g carbs well under 35g; whole-muscle pork chops in parmesan-cream pan sauce, no starch base; budget pantry ingredients, weigh-and-divide scalable to 14; no seafood. FIT.

catalog_nearest.reason: Same protein (pork chops) but sauce is mushroom cream (no parmesan) served OVER MASHED POTATOES - different sauce family and a starch base this candidate lacks. 2/4 match. Not a dupe.

Closest adjacency: pork chops + parmesan + heavy cream. But Marry Me is a sun-dried-tomato cream (that tomato base is its signature) served over pasta/rice, i.e. tomato-cream flavor family and a high-carb starch. This candidate is a plain onion-garlic-parmesan cream, basil, NO tomato, NO starch. Different dinner - flag as borderline-adjacent for the decider.

dupe_check.verdict: Not a catalog duplicate. No creamy-parmesan pork chop skillet without a starch base exists in the pork lane.

cross_protein_collision: Structurally 'creamy parmesan [protein] skillet, no starch.' A chicken or turkey 'creamy parmesan skillet' candidate in another lane would be the same dish with a swapped protein - decider should watch the chicken/turkey pools. Note: accepted creamy-tuscan-chicken-skillet is sun-dried-tomato/spinach cream, a different sauce, so no collision there.
borderline_reason: Adjacent to marry-me-pork-chops-over-pasta on the parmesan-cream axis; distinguished by absence of sun-dried tomato and absence of pasta/rice starch. Kept flagged for audit rather than silently cut.
